fault.expect: insert goal in collision: the marker's middle at the insert depth puts its end through the cup floor

rounds.diagnosis: The insert subgoal has no collision-free pose because the inside-the-interior term is applied to marker.body_center rather than to the end of the marker that goes in. With body_center pinned near/below cup.interior_center the marker's lower end (body_tip) is driven 7.5 cm below interior_center, i.e. through the cup bottom into the table, so every sample collides. Re-pick the stage's call #2 point to marker.body_tip, matching the stated goal ('body_tip inside the cup near cup.interior_center'): the tip then sits inside the interior while the rest of the marker rises out through the opening, giving a feasible, collision-free standing pose with the existing vertical-orientation row and path rows unchanged.

The transport stage's subgoal constrains the marker's lateral (up) axis to the cup axis, so the marker ends lying horizontally across the opening instead of standing over it. The insert stage then has to perform the entire 90 deg swing-up right at the cup mouth (its own path samples at roll +45/+90 already collide with the cup) and its path leaves roll completely free to permit this. Constraining marker.+front parallel to cup.up_axis at the align subgoal gives a pre-insert pose with the marker's long axis along the cup axis, matching the insert goal orientation and reducing the insertion to a straight descent.

The insert stage's path region constrains only one tilt direction: 'marker.lateral_axis perpendicular cup.up_axis' bounds pitch to +/-15 deg but leaves roll free (path image shows the marker at +45 deg and only collision keeps +90 deg out). Insertion needs the marker's long axis held near the cup axis for the whole descent. Rewrite the stage with a path rotation row that keeps the marker's long axis (marker.front_axis) parallel to cup.up_axis at a moderate tolerance, so both roll and pitch stay small while the tip enters and travels down the mouth.
